correctness.rationale: The one-point extension is possible exactly for a triangle-free neighborhood. Splitting on a nonempty selection from C leaves a complete rectangle of deletion edges between the selected portions of A and B; the known nonzero factor (1+z)^c−1 makes all same-triple polynomial fibres independent of c≥1. Accounting for empty shores and singleton shores gives D_F, correcting each doubled single edge once. The remaining rectangles have a minimum size of four and their degree-four count equals the C4 count, hence the first correction at degree five. When they are absent, the quadratic coefficient recovers m and substitution y=1+z recovers the combined degree multiplicities. For the threshold, singleton shores depend only on m. For (2,2) the star and matching are separated and star orientations exchange the shores. For (2,3), row-single counts u≥v and double count w give an exhaustive list, with mixed polynomial z((1+z)^(u+w)+(1+z)^(v+w)−2)+z²((1+z)^w−1). There are two nonsingleton fibres, at m=2 and m=4. The former gives the claimed witnesses: their degree-cube sums differ by 6 for all c, and C makes both connected. The latter uses complements of the first two patterns; both surviving A∪B graphs are P3 plus two isolated vertices. Adjoining C preserves their isomorphism. The amended verification notes accurately distinguish the original C4-free fibre check from the all-pattern analytic table. A clean independent census of 110 labelled patterns, including all 11 C4-bearing patterns through a+b=5, corroborates the table.
residual_risks: The threshold compares ordinary nonisomorphic graphs with fixed common shore sizes. It is not a claim about all patterns without forgetting shore labels, or a global threshold for Henson parameter graphs.
The inverse degree theorem applies when both deletion patterns have no C4; the amended four-edge example illustrates why the two formulations of uniqueness must be separated.

value.rationale: The inverse theorem gives a complete numerical fibre classification on a motivated structural class; the first coefficient of failure is exactly tied to a graph motif.
